turn.content:
The quantities billed here (4/18/1/4) exactly equal GR-2026-0221A's quantities. GR-B (2026-09-20) received a second, identical batch — but there is no evidence in the ledger that GR-B's goods were already billed. Key arithmetic: PO is 8/36/2/8; total received is 8/36/2/8 (both GRs). The earlier invoice MUA26090156 (2026-09-08) came 1 day after GR-A and totals the same, so it billed GR-A's 4/18/1/4. This invoice bills 4/18/1/4 again — total invoiced would be 8/36/2/8, which exactly equals received, but the same-batch duplication pattern (identical line quantities and identical total to the prior invoice) points to GR-A being billed twice rather than GR-B being billed.

Caveat: the total-invoiced arithmetic (8/36/2/8) fits within receipts, which is the `separate_delivery` signature; but separate_delivery requires a receipt for *this* delivery and the billing to be of the later delivery's quantities — and here the quantities match GR-A identically, as does the total of the prior invoice. Recorded receipts show two identical batches, so the records technically allow either reading. Given the exact same total and quantities as the already-issued invoice one day after GR-A, the dominant evidence is resubmission of the same delivery.
